title: 1975 Tan Son Nhut C-5 accident
summary: A C-5A Galaxy departed Tan Son Nhut at 16:15 heading for Clark Air Base. At 4:15 p.m. while climbing to 23000 ft over the South China Sea 13 nm off Vung Tau, the locks on the rear loading ramp failed and the cargo door opened explosively. The explosive decompression severed control cables to the tail and caused two of four hydraulic systems to fail, leaving only one aileron and spoilers. The crew performed a 180-degree turn to return to Tan Son Nhut, countering phugoid oscillations during descent. At 16:45 during final approach the descent rate increased and despite engine thrust the aircraft touched down in a rice paddy and broke up.
probable_cause: Failure of cargo door locks from inadequate maintenance combined with loss of flight control authority during approach.

factors.evidence: the locks on the rear loading ramp failed, causing the cargo door to open explosively
explosive decompression, temporarily filling the cabin with a whirlwind of fog and debris
The blowout severed control cables to the tail
the plane touched down at 4:45 p.m. in a rice paddy, and skidded for a quarter of a mile (400 m), became airborne again
Maintenance records showed that some locks from other C-5s had been cannibalized for spares and improperly refitted

events.text: The C-5A was over the South China Sea climbing to an altitude of 23000 ft when the locks on the rear loading ramp failed.
The cargo door opened explosively, causing explosive decompression that severed control cables to the tail.
Two of four hydraulic systems failed including those for the rudder and elevator, leaving only one aileron, spoilers and power.
The crew performed a 180-degree turn in order to return to Tan Son Nhut.
The aircraft began to exhibit phugoid oscillations but the crew countered them and maintained a controlled descent.
While turning on final approach, the plane's descent rate suddenly began to increase rapidly despite crew efforts.
The plane touched down at 4:45 p.m. in a rice paddy, skidded for a quarter mile, became airborne again for another half mile crossing the Saigon River, then hit a dike and broke up into four pieces.

title: Eastern Air Lines 66
summary: Flight 66 descended through a microburst on approach to JFK in severe weather, striking approach lights 2400 ft from the runway threshold. The captain was aware of wind-shear reports from preceding aircraft but continued the approach, relying on visual cues rather than instruments.
probable_cause: The aircraft's encounter with adverse winds associated with a very strong thunderstorm resulted in high descent rate into non-frangible approach light towers. The flight crew's reliance upon visual cues rather than flight instrument reference contributed to delayed recognition. Contributing was the failure of air traffic control and the flight crew to abort the landing given severe weather conditions.

factors.evidence: aircraft entered a microburst or wind shear environment caused by the severe storms
A severe thunderstorm arrived at JFK just as Flight 66 was approaching the New York City area
flight crew's delayed recognition and correction of the high descent rate
crew's reliance upon visual cues rather than on flight instrument reference
Captain was aware of reports of severe wind shear but decided to continue the approach
aircraft struck the approach lights approximately 2400 ft from the threshold of the runway

events.text: Flight 66 contacted JFK approach controller and was sequenced into pattern for Runway 22L
Controller warned all incoming aircraft of a severe wind shift on final approach
Flight crew continued approach to Runway 22L despite receiving warnings of severe weather
Aircraft entered microburst environment on final approach and struck approach lights

title: Agadir air disaster
summary: A Royal Air Maroc Boeing 707 flight from Paris to Agadir crashed into a mountain on August 3, 1975 while descending to land at Inezgane Airport. The aircraft was flying over the Atlas Mountains in heavy fog. The right wingtip and number 4 engine struck a peak about 45 miles northeast of Agadir at 2400 feet altitude. The aircraft lost control and crashed into a valley. All 188 passengers and crew aboard were killed, making it the deadliest crash involving a Boeing 707.
probable_cause: The cause of the crash was determined to be pilot error in not ensuring positive course guidance before beginning descent. The aircraft had not followed the usual north-south corridor generally used for flights to Agadir and was flying from the northeast over the Atlas Mountains.

factors.evidence: The aircraft had not followed the usual north-south corridor generally used for flights to Agadir.
There was heavy fog in the area and the aircraft was flying over the Atlas Mountains in thick fog.
The aircraft was descending from 8,000 feet and its right wingtip and number 4 engine struck a peak at 2400 feet altitude.
The aircraft struck a peak and the aircraft lost control and crashed into a valley.

events.text: The 707 left Le Bourget Airport in Paris with 181 passengers and 7 crew members
As the 707 was descending from 8,000 feet for a runway 29 approach, its right wingtip and number 4 engine struck a peak
Part of the wing separated and the aircraft lost control and crashed into a valley about 1800 feet below
Rescue teams found wreckage over a wide area and nothing bigger than 10 square feet in size
